stemBlocks.value: Rewrite the quadratic expression 4x² + 24x + 11 by completing the square, in the form a(x + h)² + k.
Think first: Pull the 4 out of the x-terms first so that the bracket starts with a plain x².

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p102-q07 from workbook page 102.

solutionSteps.instruction: Factor 4 out of the terms containing x.
Complete the square inside the bracket.

contentBlocks.value: half of 6 is 3, and 3² = 9, so x² + 6x = (x + 3)² − 9

strategyBlocks.value: Factor 4 from 4x² + 24x, complete the square inside, then expand the 4 back through and simplify the constant.

whyThisWorks.value: The square (x + 3)² reproduces x² + 6x plus an unwanted 9, so that 9 must be subtracted to keep the expression unchanged. Because the whole bracket is multiplied by 4, the correction becomes −36, not −9. The completed form shows at once that the smallest value of the expression is −25, reached when x = −3.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing 4(x + 3)² − 9 + 11, forgetting that the −9 is inside the bracket being multiplied by 4.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing 4(x + 3)² − 9 + 11, forgetting that the −9 is inside the bracket being multiplied by 4.

commonErrors.misconception: Losing the sign on the 11 when combining constants.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Losing the sign on the 11 when combining constants.

examTip.value: Write the factored bracket on its own line before completing the square — crowding both moves onto one line is where most sign errors start.
